_README: R267 / round-32 Q6 — THE THIRD REMINDER CHANNEL: A CARD THE POOL DOES NOT CARRY.
R248 read the pool's own {i}(...) reminder spans. R252 added the Algomancy
Manual for the markers no card reminds you about. Both are BASE-GAME channels,
and that is the gap this file closes: the Light & Dark expansion has neither a
manual nor (for its player counters) a printed reminder in our transcribed pool,
so every L&D-only row was structurally guaranteed to fall through to the
authored sentence no matter what the game actually said.
It said something. The designer posts cards to his own $card bot library, and
the Rot Counter card is one of them. Its text is quoted verbatim, with a date,
in data/rules/Light-and-Dark-Provisional-Glossary.md — which is where the owner was
pointing when he answered round-32 Q6 with 'Rot has now been added'.
WEAKER THAN THE OTHER TWO, DELIBERATELY, AND THE GUARD SAYS SO. The pool is
machine-readable and the manual is the game's own rules document; this is a
screenshot of a card in a Discord bot, transcribed by us into a file whose own
corpus record is labelled 'unofficial, outdated_risk: true'. So the
admissibility bar is R252 §4's, applied one channel over: the entry must be a
CONTIGUOUS VERBATIM QUOTE attributed to a named card with a date, and
test/245-printed-reminder-reach.test.ts re-derives every sentence here out of
the checked-in Rules file so that nothing in it can be paraphrased. What the
guard proves is that we transcribed the card faithfully. It does NOT prove the
card is in the current print run, and no reader of this file should think it
does.
PRINTED (pool) BEATS MANUAL BEATS CARD LIBRARY BEATS AUTHORED. This channel is
consulted only when the first two are silent, which today is one row.

Rot.text: At the start of deployment, you take damage equal to the number of rot you have. Rot does not go away.
